title: Grandparent ties can function as social infrastructure before they become formal care
source_unit: Pew Research Center synthesis using Census SIPP, University of Michigan HRS, Census ACS, and Pew surveys

observations.method: Pew analysis of U.S. Census Bureau Survey of Income and Program Participation.
observations.uncertainty: Grandparent status does not measure relationship quality, care, support, or household welfare.
observations.counterinterpretation: A high prevalence of grandparenthood does not imply that grandparents are available or able to provide support.

regular_care_100_hours_plus.unit: percent reporting 100 or more hours of grandchild/great-grandchild care over two years

observations.method: Pew analysis of the University of Michigan Health and Retirement Study.
observations.uncertainty: The two-year window overlaps the coronavirus pandemic and does not identify necessity, burden, or current care intensity.
observations.subgroup: U.S. grandparents, primarily ages 50 and older
observations.counterinterpretation: Reported care can coexist with closeness, obligation, occasional help, or substantial burden; the aggregate does not distinguish them.

denominator.unit: U.S. children, grandparents ages 65 and older, or adults with a living grandparent depending on measure

grandparent_contact_monthly_or_more.unit: percent of grandparents ages 65 and older

extremely_or_very_close.unit: percent of adults with one or more grandparents

black_extremely_or_very_close.unit: percent of Black adults with one or more grandparents

observations.method: Pew analysis of Census ACS and Pew Research Center surveys conducted in 2025.
observations.uncertainty: These are different populations and measures; contact includes seeing, phone, or texting and closeness is self-reported.
observations.subgroup: U.S. children, older grandparents, and adults with living grandparents
observations.counterinterpretation: Contact or closeness does not establish support quality, cultural identity, health, work, or consumer outcomes.

related_sources.claim: Pew source reports grandparent prevalence, caregiving, shared housing, contact, and closeness measures.

boundary: This record keeps grandparent status, routine contact, caregiving, shared housing, and reported closeness separate. It does not establish causal effects, support quality, burden, cultural identity, household welfare, or later durability.
